newsitem.title: RWANDA: Aid workers cross into eastern Zaire from Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Aid workers cross into eastern Zaire from Rwanda.

text.p: Foreign aid workers reached the eastern Zairean city of Goma on Monday with emergency medical and food supplies and a U.N. team entered the Zairean town of Bukavu to the south.

Samantha Bolton, spokeswoman for Medecins sans Frontieres (MSF-Doctors Without Borders), said vehicles from the U.N. Children's Fund, Concern, Save the Children, MSF, Care and Merlin reached Goma from the Rwandan border town of Gisenyi.
"They got thoroughly searched (by rebel forces) at the border and they only took in emergency food supplies for patients in hospitals and enough drugs to treat them," Bolton said.
"Full-scale operations will only go ahead after they have made their security assessments, in a day or two," she added in the Rwandan capital Kigali.

An official with the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs said a U.N. assessment team also reached the town of Bukavu, south of Goma, from Rwanda but added an initial report a second U.N. assessemt team had arrived in Goma on Monday was wrong.

The last foreign aid workers in eastern Zaire were evacuated from Goma more than a week ago in a lull in battles for the city between rebel forces and Zairean troops backed by Rwandan Hutu hardliners.
Bukavu is also held by rebel forces. More than a million Rwandan refugees and tens of thousands of Zaireans have been uprooted by a three-week-old rebel offensive in eastern Zaire.
The Rwandan government on Sunday gave the go ahead for some aid to reach eastern Zaire from its territory but still wants the bulk of aid to come to Rwanda in a bid to coax the refugees to come home.
